name: Loom
tagline: Async screen recording with instant hosting, transcripts, and team sharing

pricing.notes: Official/Atlassian pricing checked 2026-07-30; Business listed around $18/user/month.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan allows 25 videos of up to 5 minutes each.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Up to 50 workspace members; 25 videos/person; 5 minutes/video; unlimited-length meeting recordings; 720p.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited videos and recording length; paid Creator/Admin seat.

tiers.name: Business + AI
tiers.limits: Unlimited videos and length plus AI workflows; 14-day trial.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users and limits; price not public.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 50 workspace members, 25 videos per person, 5 minutes per video, unlimited-length meeting recordings, unlimited screenshots and 720p recording.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (about 17% off); 14-day Business + AI trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Creator and Admin roles are paid; Creator Lite is free. Seat counting and billing mechanics differ between direct Loom subscriptions and Atlassian subscriptions.

verdictSummary: Local screen recording is easy, but instant hosting, permissions, viewer analytics, comments, trimming, and team libraries push it beyond one sitting.
coreLoopDIY: Record screen and camera, encode video, upload to storage, generate transcript/summary, and serve a share page.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because a Loom link works everywhere and preserves context for the team.

priorArt.name: OBS Studio
priorArt.desc: Excellent open-source recording engine; hosting/sharing remains the DIY gap.

alternatives.name: Cap
alternatives.desc: Loom with your own storage and your own server chores.

rejectedAlternatives.name: OBS Studio
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Records anything beautifully; hosts, transcribes and organizes absolutely nothing.

notes: Classic paid-for-polish case: the local primitive is free, the workflow is subscription.
prompt:
Build me a screen-record-and-share tool to replace Loom on macOS. Requirements:

- Two parts: a local recording CLI and a share server on my own VPS.
- Recording: `rec start` / `rec stop` wrapping ffmpeg's avfoundation capture,
  screen plus mic, saved to ~/Recordings/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.mp4. No camera bubble.
- On stop: transcode to web-friendly H.264, transcribe with whisper.cpp, then
  upload video and transcript to the server with rsync over SSH.
- The server (Node + Express + better-sqlite3 behind my existing reverse proxy)
  serves each recording at an unguessable /v/<random-id> URL: player, title, date,
  and the transcript below it, searchable in-page.
- `rec stop` ends by printing the share URL and copying it to my clipboard. Target:
  under a minute from stop to link for a 2-minute video.
- The index page listing all recordings stays private (localhost or VPN only); the
  share pages are link-only, no listing anywhere. No accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: viewer analytics, comments, trimming, and team libraries. The
  unlisted URL is the entire permission model.
- README: macOS screen-recording and mic permissions, finding the right ffmpeg
  device index, and the server deploy steps.
